Environmental targets for NGCC cases [24] [25] [26] NGCC Pollutant Control Technology (lb/MWh-gross) SO 0.90 Low sulfur content fuel 2 NOx 0.43 Dry low NOx burners and SCR PM (Filterable) N/A N/A Hg N/A N/A HCl N/A N/A The NGCC cases were designed to achieve approximately 1.8 ppmv NOx emissions (referenced to 15 percent O ) through the use of a dry low NOx (DLN) burner in the combustion turbine- 2 generator (CTG)—the DLN burners reduce the emissions to about 9 ppmvd [34] (referenced to 15 percent O )—and an SCR. [35] 2 While state-of-the-art 2017 F-class and H-class CTs alone produce NOx emissions below the limit shown in Exhibit 2-14, an SCR was included to ensure the plant met EPA’s PSD program by installing BACT. The SCR system is designed for 85–87 percent NOx reduction while firing natural gas. The total sulfur content of natural gas is typically limited by contract terms and industry practice to between 0.25 and 1.00 gr/100 scf with the average total sulfur content being 0.34 gr/100 scf. [23] For this report, the natural gas was assumed to contain the average value of total sulfur of 0.34 gr/100 scf (4.71x10-4 lb-S/MMBtu). It was also assumed that the added mercaptan (CH S) 4 was the sole contributor of sulfur to the natural gas. The CH S concentration of the natural gas 4 is provided in Exhibit 2-6 as 5.75x10-6 percent by mole (mol%) (7.06x10-4 lb-CH S/MMBtu). 4 The natural gas sulfur content results in SO emissions for the non-capture case of 0.006 2 lb/MWh-gross. The CO capture system removes virtually all SO from the flue gas, resulting in 2 2 zero (reported) emissions in the capture case. The pipeline natural gas was assumed to contain no PM, Hg, or HCl. 45 COST AND PERFORMANCE BASELINE FOR FOSSIL ENERGY PLANTS VOLUME 1: BITUMINOUS COAL AND NATURAL GAS TO ELECTRICITY Under the assumptions established in Section 2.4.2, no additional control technology considerations are required for compliance with the ELG rule. 2.4.4 Carbon Dioxide EPA promulgated a New Source Performance Standard on October 23, 2015, for emissions of CO for new fossil fuel-fired electric utility generating units. [36] The limit set by the regulation 2 was 1,000 lb-CO /MWh-gross for NGCC, and 1,400 lb-CO /MWh-gross for PC and IGCC plants. 2 2 As of the publication of this report, EPA has proposed changes that increase the CO emissions 2 limit for the PC and IGCC plants considered in this study to 1,900 lb-CO /MWh-gross. [37] The 2 changes do not impact the previously established emissions limit for NGCC plants. For the IGCC cases that have CO capture, the basis is a nominal 90 percent carbon removal rate 2 based on carbon input from the coal and excluding carbon that exits the gasifier with the slag.
